subject: Re: Upgrade safety net & prioritized bundle recommendations
messages:

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Upgrade safety net & prioritized bundle recommendations

Hi Sofia / Elliot —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call, I pulled together a short set of options that let Brightline test higher throughput (multi-model routing) without losing access to key features you need (per-route tracing, KV cache). The goal is to propose a migration path that reduces your per-token costs while keeping a rollback path if latency/regression shows up.

Attached: a prioritization matrix (rows = features, columns = impact & risk) and a first-draft safety-net playbook.

Quick summary:
- Option A (Pilot burst): Keep current Tier B seats + add a Dedicated burst pool for peak hours. Low dev lift, fast to enable; saves ~18–22% token spend on peak.
- Option B (Slim bundle): Move non-critical features (long-term storage of traces, extended eval retention) to an add-on; convert base tier to a compact model profile with quantized variants. Medium risk — requires a short QA window. Estimated 26% cost reduction.
- Option C (Full upgrade): Upgrade to a throughput-focused tier and migrate heavy embedding/recall flows to a separate embedding-only endpoint. Highest savings but the longest rollout.

We recommend starting with Option A + a 2-week canary for the Slim bundle changes on a subset of routes. If the canary shows no quality degradation, we phase in the Slim bundle for the next renewal. If there are regressions, the safety-net allows an automated fallback to the prior model/version.

Next steps I propose:
1) You approve Option A pilot and tell us two sample routes to include.
2) We schedule a 30-min implementation sync next week (engineer + CS).
3) We run canary for 7–14 days and share tracing + token-cost delta.

Thanks — I attached the matrix for your review.

—
Markus Klein

Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upgrade safety net & prioritized bundle recommendations

Markus —

Appreciate the concise options and attachments. A few clarifying q's from Elliot and me after scanning the matrix:

- For Option A, can you confirm if burst capacity charges are billed separately or amortized into our existing committed spend? We want to avoid surprise overages.
- For the Slim bundle, which user-facing features are at highest risk during quantization? Elliot is particularly worried about hallucination increases on our clinical note summarization model.
- If we do the canary, what metrics will you provide? We need latency P95, API error rate, and an automated quality regression report on our baseline prompt set.

If you can answer those, we can sign off on the pilot routes. We suggest including:
- /api/v1/summarize (high priority, low volume)
- /api/v1/triage-sim (medium priority, bursty)

Thanks — happy to get this moving.

Sofia Ramos
VP Product | Brightline Health
sofia@brightlinehealth.com
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@brightlinehealth.com>, Elliot Shaw <elliot.shaw@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upgrade safety net & prioritized bundle recommendations

Thanks — quick answers below.

- Billing for Option A: burst capacity is charged as a usage add-on against your committed Dedicated pool; it’s metered and presented separately on the invoice line (so it won't change your committed spend commitments). I added a cap option we can enable so it never exceeds a fixed monthly amount.

- Slim bundle & quantization: the most sensitive functions are long-form summarization and few-shot prompting where context fidelity matters. For our quantized model profiles we include a rollback tag and a hidden A/B flag so we can keep traffic split and immediately revert if we detect a regen on the prompt set. Rishi will include recommended prompt substitutions to stabilize outputs when running quantized variants.

- Canary metrics: P95 latency, median latency, 5xx rate, token-unit cost delta, and an automated quality delta computed against your canonical prompt set (we'll run Rouge/ROUGE-L and a small human sampling for edge cases). We’ll provide a dashboard link and a weekly summary PDF.

Lauren and Ben — can your teams prepare the canary runbook and enable the cap on burst billing? I put an initial estimate in the matrix for a 2-week canary starting Mar 8 if Brightline approves.

On billing cap options: we can set a hard cap or an alert-only cap; I recommend alert+hard cap for this account given their sensitivity.

—
Markus
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Sofia / Elliot —

We can run the pilot as Markus described. Action items we’ll take on immediately if you approve:
1) Ben: configure burst pool + hard cap and confirm invoice line formatting (Ben: please reply with cap cadence).
2) Rishi: export the canary QA prompt set and prepare quantized-model prompts with substitution guidance.
3) Ops: create the canary runbook and the dashboard share (read-only).

Ben, Rishi — can you drop short ETA replies here? Sofia, if you’re comfortable with the schedule, we’ll lock Mar 8 start and share the Drive doc with explicit rollback play steps.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
